name: GSK-2849466

lead: GSK-2849466 is a SARM from GlaxoSmithKline studied for cachexia and heart failure, which muscle-focused readers note as a lean-mass candidate.

It belongs to the N-arylhydroxyalkyl class and is meant to activate androgen receptors preferentially in muscle and bone rather than reproductive tissue. A Phase I trial begun in 2012 tested safety, tolerability and pharmacokinetics in 17 healthy men, after which development was discontinued. No appearance-related data exist.

paras: It is not marketed, and no routine for physique use exists.
No trial results are published in the sources reviewed. The SARM class is unapproved, banned by WADA, and associated in case reports with liver injury from recreational use.

angle.text: GSK-2849466 is a SARM investigated for cachexia and heart failure, noted by muscle-focused readers as a lean-mass candidate. It is meant to activate androgen receptors in muscle and bone. Development stopped after one small Phase I trial in 17 healthy men.

lead: GSK-2849466 (GSK2849466) is an investigational non-steroidal selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) of the N-arylhydroxyalkyl class, developed by GlaxoSmithKline and investigated for cachexia and heart failure [1][2].

A Phase I trial begun in 2012 evaluated its safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics in 17 healthy male subjects [2]. Development was discontinued after Phase I [1]. No appearance-related data are available.

paras: Wikipedia lists GSK2849466 as a Phase I candidate that was discontinued [1]. Its registered trial, NCT01696604, started on 26 September 2012, enrolled 17 healthy men, and is listed as completed, with cachexia as the associated condition [2].

No SARM had been approved by the FDA or EMA as of 2023. Enobosarm increased lean body mass in Phase III trials without significantly improving physical function, and WADA has prohibited the class since 2008 [1].

One Phase I trial (NCT01696604, n=17, healthy males, 2012) assessed safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics and is listed as completed [2]. Results are not available in the sources reviewed, and no efficacy trial has been reported.

timeline.event: Phase I trial in healthy males begins. [2]
